name: OA Stability Check
description: Verify OA runtime, automation and actual Dot tool calls on JO through current owners, focused evidence, minimal authorized canaries and reconciled cleanup.
content:
OA Stability Check

Verify that Obsidian Agent (OA), its automation and development routes, and the tools its actual Dot callers use work end to end on JO, Josiah's Personal Windows workstation with Ubuntu WSL. Run this after a restart, host update, deployment, credential change, or addition to OA. Start from the OA folder in WSL. Inspect the installed runtime and an allowed isolated checkout when source is needed. Keep the dirty primary checkout outside the read and write scope.

Build a finite check from current OA configuration, installed service definitions, registered routes, connected tool grants, and existing run receipts. Include new OA-owned components as they appear. Verify expected capabilities rather than a fixed tool count or historical release. Read the original repair/check owner and its exact receipts first; do not duplicate active work, deployments, pending questions, Stops, or uncertain effects.

## Keep the check small and meaningful

- Reuse qualified receipts when their exact target, source revision, account, host, route, permissions and behavior still apply. Label fresh observations, cached observations, historical receipts, blocked checks and untested checks separately. Refresh only the missing evidence or changed boundary.
- Prefer a harmless current read through the real granted tool when it proves the required capability. An authenticated read, schema discovery, preview, fixture, accepted dispatch, completed live model turn and verified external effect are different evidence. Never promote one into another.
- For necessary model canaries, use the smallest adequate available model and effort supported by that route's current catalog. Honor an explicit user model, effort or speed choice instead of substituting it. Record requested, resolved and observed choices, including the actual speed/tier field; do not infer price or capability from catalog order or a model's name.
- Use one short turn or the smallest representative operation per distinct required boundary, with an expected result and bounded timeout. Avoid repeated model variants, broad datasets, unnecessary files and new dependencies. Use focused relevant checks and existing qualified receipts; do not rerun a giant unchanged suite as a routine stability check. Mandatory repository delivery checks and CI still apply when a repair is actually delivered.
- Use live canaries only within the current authorization for model usage and effects. A prior policy denial stays blocked until its supported owner provides materially new, relevant evidence. Do not retry around it through another host, provider, permission mode or network route, weaken security, or interpret an authentication status as clearance.

## Required live retained Dot to Claude Code check

Every stability run requires a fresh, single-turn, no-write canary from the retained Dot to Personal WSL Claude Code (`P-L-Claude`). Verify the actual retained authority, account, host, environment and client through `oa_read_capabilities`, then read the current Project context. Confirm the existing launch grant and the trusted registered checkout for the exact Project, repository and route. Use `oa_launch_managed_local` with the fixed `kind: route-check`, those three destination IDs and one stable operation ID. Select the smallest adequate supported model and effort only when the fixed interface accepts those controls. Otherwise use the route default. Record the requested, resolved and observed model, effort and speed or tier as available, and mark missing fields unknown.

Use `oa_launch_status` with `managed=true` under the original operation ID, then `oa_result_read` for that outcome. A pass requires both a succeeded original outcome with its checked checkout and a completed native turn for the same Claude Code session. Record the operation, outcome, native session and turn IDs and the checked checkout revision. Keep authentication, catalog discovery, fixture results, queued acknowledgments and earlier turns separate from this run's proof. A missing grant, unverified trusted checkout or absent or unresolved completion receipt leaves the required check blocked or unverified and holds the overall pass. Dispatch once on the bound route. Reconcile uncertainty only under the original operation identity and preserve existing permissions and Stops.

## Check the actual owners and entrypoints

1. Verify Windows and WSL agree on JO and the selected environment. Check the boot/sign-in timeline when relevant, the hidden launcher and supervised WSL child, published revision, installed pin, loaded processes, and release served on loopback and Tailscale. Trace a mismatch to the first differing owner. A clean pin or HTTP success alone does not prove current loaded code or every integration.

2. Inventory OA-owned Windows scheduled tasks, systemd services/timers and cron jobs. Read actual triggers, last outcomes, locks, retry/backoff and fresh end-to-end receipts. Follow Telemetry from collection through publication and served data. Check Vault Sync, Gmail and other registered integrations through their existing owners. When fresh proof is missing, use the next scheduled occurrence or a safe existing owner check; do not create a second poller, perpetual monitor or new automation just to test one.

3. Verify credentials through the paths the automations actually use: password-manager/broker readiness, configured account sign-ins, token renewal and personal Git access from the real runner. Expose only status and expected-identity matches. Do not read or print secret values, private credential files, process environments or message bodies as diagnostics. Keep organization SSO off JO.

4. Discover the current granted tools and callable schemas from the actual retained Dot/client, and compare them with the installed descriptor and owning operation. Exercise supported read arguments and current context reads for approved folders, then verify the returned source IDs, revisions, freshness and omissions. Tool names, installation or advertised schema fields alone do not prove the caller can invoke them. If discovery differs, use only the supported refresh mechanism and read back both discovery and an actual call.

5. Cover the named integrations through their real owners, plus any other currently registered in-scope tools:
   - Telegram: verify the single poll owner, recent successful progress, failure-window versus current-burst state, offset/request ownership, retry/backoff and duplicate-poller evidence. Do not reset cursors or send/poll directly as a diagnostic. Any authorized message canary needs its exact recipient, effect receipt and result; a healthy poll is not proof of message processing or delivery.
   - Todoist: verify the intended account, exact task/Project association and real task/context read behavior using current returned data shapes. Preserve recurrence, due dates, completion and original task identities. Do not complete, move or create real tasks as test fixtures; use a disposable owned task only when that exact effect and cleanup are authorized.
   - OpenClaw: check the configured integration through its existing readiness and execution owners, distinguishing Gateway, harness, provider authentication and an actual result. Resolve the user's name OpenCloud against the actual registry: if it names another component or has no verified mapping, report the unresolved identity rather than silently treating it as OpenClaw.
   - Claude and Codex: check native Windows and WSL routes, effective permissions and approval behavior, trusted folders, Project/checkout mappings, current model catalogs and route readiness. Existing mappings and admitted choices stay with their owners. Authentication, CLI presence, a startup request and a completed live turn are separate; stored history access does not prove live desktop attachment.
   - Dots and applicable ChatGPT Work connections: identify the actual caller, account, host and surface. Verify that caller's current granted tools, approved-folder context and supported provider controls. Desktop, browser, phone and Voice access need their own evidence; local Codex/MCP configuration does not prove another Dot's inventory or loading.

6. Follow each exercised path to its owning receipt and after-state. For native events, distinguish subscription, callback receipt, actual Dot processing, an answer and human acceptance. A queued command or callback is not a completed workflow. Reconcile timeouts or lost acknowledgments under the original operation identity before retry, continuation, cleanup or any alternative route. Resolve a pending question from already recorded facts through its supported owner; genuinely missing human input blocks only that dependent action.

## Reconcile and clean up the canaries

Track exact resources created by this check in the working context. After a settled canary, use supported cleanup only for reconciled, exact owned disposable artifacts, records, sessions and temporary processes, then verify removal. Preserve concise evidence and original owner receipts. Do not erase shared logs, clear unrelated caches, delete user data, stop existing services/work, undo real task history or replace mappings. An unknown effect must be reconciled before cleanup; retain its identity and report any residual or blocked cleanup instead of claiming success.

Apply only authorized, in-scope recovery through the affected owner and verify it through the original entrypoint. A busy bridge, active work or independent Stop keeps its owner; report the supported deferred action rather than forcing a restart. Continue independent checks when an item needs sign-in, a scheduled occurrence or another device.

## Report

Return a concise component/tool/route table with the expected capability, actual call or receipt, observation time and source revision, evidence class, pass/fail/blocked/untested result, and cleanup/residual state. Separate installed delivery from actual use and human acceptance. State any repair and its verified result, exact model/executor for live turns, and the smallest remaining owner action or evidence. Do not claim whole-system stability from a sample or manufacture acceptance.

USER CONTEXT, GOAL, OR NOTES BELOW. IGNORE IF BLANK.
